page: Microsoft Azure F48as_v7 belongs to the compute-optimized Fasv7 family, powered by a 48-core dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at frequencies up to 4.5 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture without simultaneous multithreading, each vCPU maps to a single physical core, coupled with 192.0 GB of total system RAM (4.0 GB per core). The processor integrates 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, complemented by advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 (F, VNNI, BF16), AVX-VNNI, and hardware cryptography extensions such as VAES and SHA-NI.

Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier processing power and memory performance. In stress-ng evaluations, the server produced scores of 3,793.98 in single-core and 176,853.77 in multi-core execution. PassMark testing further demonstrates high compute capabilities, logging a CPU score of 98,684.41 and an extended instructions score of 116,704.76. Data compression throughput reached 41.1 GB/sec for single-threaded gzip and 674.49 GB/sec for multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Cached small-block read bandwidth peaked at 9,266.23 GB/sec, supporting high throughput in data operations, evidenced by 130.33 million Redis SET operations per second.

The F48as_v7 does not bundle local disk storage and contains no discrete GPU accelerators. Consequently, all persistent data depends on attached remote storage volumes. For machine learning, CPU-driven inference remains efficient on small and medium models, achieving 353.14 tokens per second on 135M models and 56.8 tokens per second on 7B models, though throughput falls to median levels on 70B parameter models. Given its dedicated high-frequency core density and balanced 1:4 core-to-RAM ratio, the instance provides cost-effective compute performance for batch simulations, software compilation, web serving, in-memory caching tiers, and relational database management.
description: The Microsoft Azure F48as_v7 is a compute-optimized instance equipped with 48 dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 physical cores operating at frequencies up to 4.5 GHz and 192.0 GB of system memory. Lacking simultaneous multithreading, each vCPU corresponds directly to a physical core with 4.0 GB of allocated RAM. The underlying processor supports AVX-512 vector extensions, VNNI, and cryptographic instruction sets. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier computational and in-memory performance, achieving 176,853.77 on stress-ng multi-core tests, 130.33 million Redis SET operations per second, and 674.49 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. The instance includes no local ephemeral storage, relying entirely on remote volumes, and contains no hardware accelerators. With strong CPU-based inference for small and medium models alongside robust data processing bandwidth, the F48as_v7 is appropriate for intensive computational simulations, caching layers, high-throughput web serving, and enterprise database workloads.
